title: Asymmetric routing triggered control-plane connection drops — investigation notes
body:
Summary:

During a customer network maintenance window on 2026-03-22 we observed a widespread loss of control-plane connectivity from the customer's on-prem agents to the Redwood control plane. Approximately 80% of agent heartbeats for that customer failed within a 20-minute window, causing nodes to be marked unhealthy and triggering local fallback behavior. The issue reoccurred intermittently for ~6 hours until a routing configuration rollback on the customer's edge devices restored symmetric paths.

Why this doc exists (working):
- Capture facts and timeline while still fresh.
- Draft an on-call runbook entry to speed future resolution for similar asymmetric-routing/firewall-state incidents.
- Propose follow-ups and code/agent hardening items.

Impact:
- Customer: degraded control-plane connectivity; automated failovers for 12 services; increased tail latency on RPCs that require control-plane checks. Business impact classified as P2 for Redwood.
- Redwood: alert noise across the private-deployments pager rotation; traffic routed to fallback model pools for affected tenants.

Detection & Alerts:
- Primary detection: control-plane upstream heartbeat failure alert (SLO: agent heartbeat loss > 5% in 5m) fired at 2026-03-22T02:12:34Z.
- Secondary signals: surge in TLS handshake retries in controlplane ingress logs, TCP retransmit spikes in BGP peer windows, and customer-reported degraded app responsiveness.

Timeline (concise):
- 02:05 UTC: Customer performs planned WAN routing change (announced in their maintenance ticket).
- 02:12 UTC: First SRE alert for increased heartbeat failures.
- 02:18 UTC: Oncall collects tcpdump from a representative agent and sees SYN/ACKs leaving but ACKs not seen on the same path (asymmetric flow indication).
- 02:30 UTC: Customer confirms they deployed a new route on ASBR that changes egress interface for control-plane traffic.
- 03:00 UTC: Mitigation attempt 1: restart agent to reestablish connections — high failure rate continues.
- 04:45 UTC: Customer rolls back the route change; heartbeats recover gradually over 20 minutes.
- 05:10 UTC: Post-recovery monitoring shows rates back to normal.

What we observed (evidence):
- Packet captures from agent-side (pcap) show outbound TLS SYN/handshake packets to control-plane IPs routed via WAN1, but the return path uses WAN2 due to asymmetric BGP policies, and WAN2 has a stateful firewall that had no established outbound state and therefore dropped return packets.
- Control-plane ingress logs show bursts of partial TLS handshakes from many sources, then resets.
- Customer firewall logs indicate interface-level policy that only allowed established flows on the WAN2 interface and dropped unsolicited inbound packets coming from control-plane IPs to agent ephemeral ports.
- No evidence of corrupted packets, MTU issues, or agent code regressions.

Root cause hypothesis (single sentence):
A customer WAN routing change introduced asymmetric routing where return traffic from Redwood control-plane egressed via a different edge interface that enforced strict stateful firewall policies; the firewall dropped the return packets because it had no corresponding outbound flow — agents could send packets but never completed TLS sessions.

Contributing factors:
- Customer's ASBR/BGP change created asymmetric paths for traffic between agent and control plane.
- Edge firewall had strict stateful policy and performed deep inspection, dropping packets that were not matched to local outbound state.
- Our standard agent reconnect logic and TCP backoff were not sufficient to hide the transient asymmetric condition (too many handshake retries, causing load on control plane).

Immediate mitigations tried (what worked / didn't):
- Agent restarts (didn't help while asymmetry persisted).
- Asking customer to open firewall for control-plane IP ranges and ephemeral ports (helpful but not permitted by customer's policy).
- Customer rollback of the routing change (successful).
- Temporary workaround we discussed: configure SNAT on the edge so return path is symmetric (customer declined initially due to internal constraints).

Longer-term mitigations and follow-ups (action items):
1) Runbook entry (owners: eng-private-deployments / eng-sre): create a dedicated triage checklist for asymmetric-routing incidents (see 'Runbook draft' section below).
2) Agent hardening (owner: controlplane-agent team): add optional STUN-like connectivity probe and fall back to persistent proxy mode (agent can use a customer-hosted relay in the same site to ensure stateful symmetry) — RFC in PR linked artifact.
3) Monitoring improvements (owner: observability): add an 'asymmetric path suspicion' signal that correlates tcpdump-derived src/dst interface mismatch with firewall-drop counts and marks incidents for faster human triage.
4) Customer onboarding docs (owner: solutions-engineering): update private deployment checklist to include explicit guidance on symmetric routing and SNAT options for edge devices.
5) Incident postmortem (owner: this doc owner): convert to formal postmortem and escalate change to product/security review if agent-level changes are required.

Runbook draft (for on-call):
- Symptoms to check quickly:
  * Large increase in agent heartbeat failures and TLS retry counters across a single customer site.
  * TCP retransmit spikes and partial handshake patterns in control-plane ingress logs.
  * Packet captures from agent host show outbound packets but lack of corresponding inbound ACKs on same interface.
- Quick triage checklist (order matters):
  1) Confirm the alert scope (single customer? single region?).
  2) Grab agent-side tcpdump (10s) with: sudo tcpdump -i any host <controlplane-ip> and port <controlplane-port> -w /tmp/agent.pcap
  3) From control-plane egress edge, request a packet capture for traffic to that customer's agent IPs.
  4) Compare src/dst interfaces and AS paths: if agent->controlplane and controlplane->agent egress interfaces differ, suspect asymmetric routing.
  5) Ask customer: did you make routing or firewall changes? Check their maintenance ticket.
  6) If customer confirms asymmetric change, recommend immediate rollback or apply SNAT to ensure symmetric flows.
  7) If rollback not possible and policy allows, recommend temporary firewall rule to allow control-plane IPs and ephemeral ports on the return interface.
  8) Escalate to network engineering and the customer's network contacts for BGP/policy fixes.

- Commands and quick queries to run:
  * On agent host: sudo ss -tnp | grep <controlplane-ip>
  * On agent host (pcap): sudo tcpdump -i any -vvv host <controlplane-ip> and port <controlplane-port> -c 200
  * On control-plane egress box: sudo tcpdump -i <egress-if> host <agent-ip> and port <agent-port> -c 200
  * traceroute/tcptraceroute: sudo mtr -z -r -c 10 <controlplane-ip> ; tcptraceroute <controlplane-ip> <port>
  * Firewall checks (ask customer): show ip conntrack | grep <agent-ip> ; show firewall logs for drops to agent ephemeral port ranges

Monitoring queries (PromQL examples for observability team):
- agent_heartbeat_failure_ratio{customer_id="ACME"} > 0.05 for 5m
- sum(rate(tcp_retransmits_total[1m])) by (customer_id)
- rate(ingress_tls_partial_handshakes_total[1m])
Add a composite alert that fires when partial_handshakes spike AND agent_heartbeat_failure_ratio spikes for the same customer.

Post-incident notes / open questions (TODOs):
- Confirm whether any other customers had similar transient issues during the same maintenance window (we saw one other minor event that might share pattern).
- Should agent use shorter keepalives to detect and rebind earlier? Tradeoff vs chattiness.
- PR #214 (linked) contains an agent-side relay prototype; schedule review with privacy/compliance before recommending customer relay.
- Document recommended ACLs for common enterprise firewalls (FortiGate, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA) to minimize friction in private deployments.

Owners and reviewers:
- Incident owner (write-up): Priya Nair (eng-private-deployments)
- Network analysis reviewer: Jordan Blake (eng-infrastructure)
- Agent changes owner: Marta Ruiz (controlplane-agent)
